cor-mvn-AY-BY.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ), and let A and B be matrices with n columns. Then AY and BY are independent iff AΣB⊤=0. In that case g(AY) and h(BY) are independent for all measurable functions g and h.

cor-mvn-marginals.title: Marginal distributions
cor-mvn-marginals.html: Every subvector of a normal vector is normal. If 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and Y1 consists of the entries with indices in a set I, then 𝛍Y1∼N(μI,ΣII), where 𝛍μI and ΣII keep the entries, rows and columns indexed by I. In particular Yi∼N(μi,σii).

cor-mvn-standardize.title: Standardization and rotation
cor-mvn-standardize.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ).

  1. If Σ is positive definite and Σ=AA⊤ with A square, then 𝛍A−1(Y−μ)∼Nn(0,I). Its entries are independent standard normal variables.

  2. If Σ=σ2I and Q is an n×n orthogonal matrix, then 𝛍Q⊤Y∼Nn(Q⊤μ,σ2I).

def-mvn.title: Multivariate normal distribution
def-mvn.html: A random vector Y=(Y1,…,Yn)⊤ has a multivariate normal distribution if a⊤Y has a univariate normal distribution (possibly degenerate) for every a∈Rn. Such a Y is also said to be jointly normal, and its entries are said to be jointly normal random variables.

def-mvn-partial-correlation.title: Partial correlation
def-mvn-partial-correlation.html: Let Y=(Y1⊤,Y2⊤)⊤ be a random vector with covariance matrix Σ, partitioned as in Section 3.5, and write Σ11⋅2=Σ11−Σ12Σ22−Σ21=(σij⋅2). The partial covariance of Yi and Yj (two entries of Y1) given Y2 is σij⋅2, and their partial correlation given Y2 is ρij⋅2=σij⋅2σii⋅2σjj⋅2, provided σii⋅2 and σjj⋅2 are positive. When the conditioning variables are Yk,Yl,… we also write ρij⋅kl…. The matrix of partial correlations is D−1/2Σ11⋅2D−1/2 with D=diag(Σ11⋅2), the correlation matrix (@def-rv-correlation) built from Σ11⋅2.

eq-mvn-conditional.html: 𝛍𝛍Y1∣Y2=y2 ∼ Nn1(μ1+Σ12Σ22−(y2−μ2), Σ11−Σ12Σ22−Σ21),

eq-mvn-density.html: 𝛍𝛍f(y)=(2π)−n/2det(Σ)−1/2exp⁡{−12(y−μ)⊤Σ−1(y−μ)},y∈Rn.

eq-mvn-linear-combination.html: 𝛍a⊤Y∼N(a⊤μ, a⊤Σa)for every a∈Rn.

eq-mvn-mgf.html: 𝛍MY(t)=exp⁡(t⊤μ+12t⊤Σt)for every t∈Rn.

eq-mvn-partial-recursion.html: ρ12⋅3=ρ12−ρ13ρ23(1−ρ132)(1−ρ232),|ρ13|<1, |ρ23|<1.

eq-mvn-random-x-model.html: 𝛃𝛃𝛔𝛃𝛍Y=α+β⊤X+e,β=ΣXX−1σXY,α=μY−β⊤μX,e∼N(0,σ2) independent of X,

exm-mvn-bivariate.title: The bivariate normal
exm-mvn-bivariate.html: For n=2, write σ12,σ22>0 for the variances and ρ for the correlation. Then Σ=(σ12ρσ1σ2ρσ1σ2σ22),detΣ=σ12σ22(1−ρ2), so Σ is positive definite iff |ρ|<1. With standardized coordinates ui=(yi−μi)/σi, the density @eq-mvn-density is f(y1,y2)=12πσ1σ21−ρ2exp⁡{−u12−2ρu1u2+u222(1−ρ2)}. When ρ=0 it factors into the two univariate normal densities. When ρ=±1 there is no density: Var(u2∓u1)=0 in standardized units, so all the probability lies on a line.

exm-mvn-longley.title: Employment and unemployment
exm-mvn-longley.html:
Longley’s macroeconomic series record, among other things, total employment and the number unemployed in the United States for the 16 years 1947–1962. Their correlation is 0.502: years with more people employed had more people unemployed. Both series grew with the population. Their correlations with the calendar year are 0.971 and 0.668. Adjusting for year, the partial correlation is −0.829. Once the common trend is removed, a year with unemployment above its trend is a year with employment below its trend, as one would expect. Figure 3.6.1 shows both scatterplots. The listing computes the partial correlation in all four ways above. They agree to ten decimal places. The slope in panel (b), −0.996, is the coefficient of unemployment in the regression of employment on unemployment and year, as @thm-proj-fwl requires. Its t statistic is −5.34.

Removing a linear time trend before correlating two series is the problem that Frisch and Waugh (1933) solved, and it is a special case of partial correlation.

exm-mvn-ls-estimator.title: Least squares under normal errors
exm-mvn-ls-estimator.html:
Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2I) with X of full column rank p, and let M=X(X⊤X)−1X⊤, the symmetric idempotent matrix of rank p with MX=X (Chapter 5 and Chapter 6). By @thm-mvn-linear:

  1. 𝛃𝛃β^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤Y∼Np(β,σ2(X⊤X)−1), a nonsingular normal vector;

  2. 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌λ⊤β^∼N(λ⊤β,σ2λ⊤(X⊤X)−1λ) for every 𝛌λ∈Rp;

  3. the fitted values 𝛃Y^=MY∼Nn(Xβ,σ2M), singular of rank p;

  4. the residuals 𝛆ε^=(I−M)Y∼Nn(0,σ2(I−M)), singular of rank n−p.

No density for Y^ or 𝛆ε^ was needed, and none exists.

exm-mvn-ls-independence.title: Coefficients and residuals
exm-mvn-ls-independence.html: In the setting of @exm-mvn-ls-estimator, 𝛃𝛆Cov(β^,ε^)=(X⊤X)−1X⊤(σ2I)(I−M)=σ2(X⊤X)−1{(I−M)X}⊤=0, since (I−M)X=0. Hence 𝛃β^ is independent of the residual vector, and so of the residual sum of squares 𝛆‖ε^‖2 and of the estimate 𝛆s2=‖ε^‖2/(n−p). The same argument shows that the fitted values Y^ and the residuals are independent. This independence is what allows a t statistic 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌(λ⊤β^−λ⊤β)/{s2λ⊤(X⊤X)−1λ}1/2 to have a t distribution (@thm-glh-t-test).

exm-mvn-mean-deviations.title: Sample mean and deviations
exm-mvn-mean-deviations.html: Let Y∼Nn(μ1,σ2I), so that Y1,…,Yn is a random sample from N(μ,σ2). The mean is Y¯=n−11⊤Y, and the vector of deviations is d=(I−n−111⊤)Y. As in @exm-rv-centering, Cov(Y¯,d)=σ2n−11⊤(I−n−111⊤)=0⊤, By @cor-mvn-AY-BY, Y¯ is independent of d, and so of every function of the deviations: the sample variance S2=‖d‖2/(n−1), the range, the sample skewness. The distribution of (n−1)S2/σ2 is found in @cor-qf-sample-variance. The computation used Cov(Y)=σ2I only through Σ1∈span(1), which is the precise condition for the conclusion (@exr-mvn-equicorrelated-mean).

exm-mvn-mixture.title: A mixture of two correlations
exm-mvn-mixture.html:
Fix 0<ρ<1. With probability 12 draw (Y1,Y2) from the bivariate normal with unit variances and correlation ρ, and otherwise from the one with correlation −ρ. Both components have N(0,1) margins, so the mixture does too, exactly. The covariance is 12ρ+12(−ρ)=0. The pair is nevertheless dependent: since E(Y12Y22)=1+2r2 for a standard bivariate normal with correlation r, the squares have correlation ρ2, not zero. The direction a=(1,1)⊤/2 exposes the failure of joint normality. S=(Y1+Y2)/2 is an equal mixture of N(0,1+ρ) and N(0,1−ρ). It has variance 1 but kurtosis ES4=32{(1+ρ)2+(1−ρ)2}=3(1+ρ2), where a normal variable would have 3.

Figure 3.3.1 shows a simulation with ρ=0.8 and 200,000 draws. Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests of normality for the two margins give p-values 0.84 and 0.29. The sample correlation is −0.0033, the correlation of the squares is 0.640 (theory 0.64), and the kurtosis of S is 4.88 (theory 4.92). The Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of S from N(0,1) is 0.067, which with this many draws rejects normality at any conventional level.

exm-mvn-overlapping-sums.title: Three overlapping sums
exm-mvn-overlapping-sums.html: Let Z∼N3(0,I) and U=(Z1+Z2, Z2−Z3, Z1+Z3)⊤. Then U=AZ with rows (1,1,0), (0,1,−1) and (1,0,1), so U is normal with mean zero and covariance AA⊤=(21112−11−12). The vector (1,−1,−1)⊤ lies in N(AA⊤), and the rank is 2. Correspondingly U1−U2−U3=0 for every outcome, not merely with probability one. Each Ui is N(0,2), each pair (Ui,Uj) has a nonsingular covariance matrix (determinant 3) and a bivariate density, and yet the triple lives on a plane.

exm-mvn-sign-flip.title: A random sign
exm-mvn-sign-flip.html: Let Z∼N(0,1) and let S be independent of Z with Pr(S=1)=Pr(S=−1)=12. Put W=SZ. By symmetry of Z, W∼N(0,1). Also Cov(Z,W)=E(S)E(Z2)=0. But Z+W=(1+S)Z equals zero with probability 12 and is otherwise N(0,4). A variable with an atom at zero and a continuous part is not normal, so (Z,W) is not jointly normal. And Z and W are far from independent: |W|=|Z| always.

exm-mvn-trivariate.title: Holding a third variable fixed
exm-mvn-trivariate.html: Let 𝛍Y∼N3(μ,Σ) with 𝛍μ=(10−1),Σ=(412132222). Conditioning Y1 on Y2 alone gives slope σ12/σ22=13 and conditional variance 113. Conditioning on (Y2,Y3), the listing computes B=Σ12Σ22−1 in exact arithmetic and finds E(Y1∣Y2=y2,Y3=y3)=3−y2+2y3,Var(Y1∣Y2,Y3)=1. The coefficient of y2 changes sign. Among outcomes with the same Y3, larger Y2 goes with smaller Y1. Across all outcomes, larger Y2 goes with larger Y1, because both tend to be large when Y3 is large. The conditional variance 1 also equals detΣ/detΣ22=2/2, as @thm-mvn-conditional(c) predicts.

exm-mvn-trivariate-partial.title: The trivariate example, continued
exm-mvn-trivariate-partial.html: For Σ of @exm-mvn-trivariate, the listing gives the covariance of (Y1,Y2) given Y3 as (2−1−11). So ρ12=0.289 while ρ12⋅3=−0.707. The script confirms that @eq-mvn-partial-recursion, @prp-mvn-precision, and the correlation of simulated residuals all give this value.

exm-mvn-two-lines.title: Two regression lines
exm-mvn-two-lines.html: Take μX=1, μY=2, σX=1, σY=1.5 and ρ=0.7. The regression of Y on X has slope 1.05 and residual standard deviation 1.071. Drawn in the same (x,y) plane, the regression of X on Y has slope 2.14, and the major axis of the ellipses lies between them, with slope 1.76. Figure 3.5.1 shows the three lines. The line E(Y∣X=x) passes through the points where each contour ellipse has a vertical tangent (@exr-mvn-tangent): on a vertical line X=x, the density is highest at the conditional mean. A least squares line fitted to 60 draws has slope 1.12 (standard error 0.16). It estimates the regression of Y on X, not the major axis.

exr-mvn-cholesky.title: A2
exr-mvn-cholesky.html: For the bivariate normal of @exm-mvn-bivariate, find the Cholesky factor L of Σ and write Y1 and Y2 in terms of two independent standard normals. Do the same with the symmetric square root when σ1=σ2=1. Why do the two representations define the same distribution?

exr-mvn-collider.title: B1
exr-mvn-collider.html: Let X, Z and e be independent, with X,Z∼N(0,1) and e∼N(0,τ2), and let C=X+Z+e. Show that ρXZ=0 but ρXZ⋅C=−1/(1+τ2). What happens as τ→0 and as τ→∞?

exr-mvn-conditional-density.title: C1
exr-mvn-conditional-density.html: Assume Σ is positive definite. Prove @thm-mvn-conditional(b) by dividing the joint density by the marginal density of Y2 directly, using the partitioned inverse and the block determinant formula.

exr-mvn-conditional-numeric.title: A1
exr-mvn-conditional-numeric.html: For 𝛍μ and Σ of @exm-mvn-trivariate, find the conditional distribution of (Y1,Y2) given Y3=y3 and of Y3 given (Y1,Y2)=(y1,y2). Verify that the conditional variances are smaller than the unconditional ones.

exr-mvn-conditional-to-joint.title: B1
exr-mvn-conditional-to-joint.html: Suppose 𝛍Y2∼N(μ2,Σ22) and that, given Y2=y2, Y1 is N(a+By2,S) with a, B and S not depending on y2. Show that (Y1⊤,Y2⊤)⊤ is jointly normal and find its mean and covariance. Explain why @exm-mvn-mixture does not contradict this.

exr-mvn-ellipse.title: A2
exr-mvn-ellipse.html: Let Σ have unit variances and correlation ρ, with |ρ|<1. Find the principal axes and half-lengths of the ellipse Δ2=c2, show that its area is πc21−ρ2, and show that it contains probability 1−e−c2/2.

exr-mvn-equicorrelated-mean.title: B1
exr-mvn-equicorrelated-mean.html: Let Y∼Nn(μ1,Σ) with Σ arbitrary. Show that Y¯ is independent of the deviations Yi−Y¯ iff Σ1∈span(1), that is, iff all row sums of Σ are equal. Check the condition for the equicorrelation matrix σ2{(1−ρ)I+ρ11⊤}, and for a two-group matrix: the first m1 and the last m2 observations form groups, all variances are 1, the correlation is ρ within a group and τ between groups.

exr-mvn-fourth-moments.title: B1
exr-mvn-fourth-moments.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) and 𝛍X=Y−μ. Expand the moment generating function of X in a power series to show that all odd-order moments of X vanish and E(XiXjXkXl)=σijσkl+σikσjl+σilσjk. Deduce that Var(X⊤AX)=2tr(AΣAΣ) for symmetric A.

exr-mvn-identify-density.title: A1
exr-mvn-identify-density.html: Show that f(y1,y2)=kexp⁡{−12(2y12+2y1y2+y22−4y1−2y2)} is a bivariate normal density for a suitable constant k. Find k, 𝛍μ, Σ and the correlation.

exr-mvn-independent-entries.title: A1
exr-mvn-independent-entries.html: Let Y1,…,Yn be independent with Yi∼N(μi,σi2). Show directly from @def-mvn that Y=(Y1,…,Yn)⊤ is multivariate normal, and find its mean and covariance. Show also that a constant vector c is Nn(c,0).

exr-mvn-linear-numeric.title: A1
exr-mvn-linear-numeric.html: Let 𝛍Y∼N3(μ,Σ) with 𝛍μ=(0,1,2)⊤ and Σ=(210121012). Find the joint distribution of U=Y1+Y2+Y3, V=Y1−Y3 and W=Y1−2Y2+Y3. Which of the pairs are independent? Is V independent of (U,W)?

exr-mvn-longley-gnp.title: B4
exr-mvn-longley-gnp.html: Using the Longley data of @exm-mvn-longley, compute the partial correlation of employment and unemployment given both year and GNP, in at least two of the four ways. Draw the corresponding residual scatterplot. Does adjusting for GNP as well as year change the conclusion?

exr-mvn-noncentral-mahalanobis.title: B3
exr-mvn-noncentral-mahalanobis.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with Σ positive definite and let 𝛎ν be a fixed vector. Show that 𝛎𝛎(Y−ν)⊤Σ−1(Y−ν) has the noncentral chi-squared distribution χ2(n,γ) with 𝛍𝛎𝛍𝛎γ=(μ−ν)⊤Σ−1(μ−ν), in the convention of @def-qf-noncentral-chisq, and find its mean.

exr-mvn-pairwise-normal.title: C1
exr-mvn-pairwise-normal.html: Let φ be the N(0,1) density, 0<ε≤e3/2, and f(x,y,z)=φ(x)φ(y)φ(z){1+εxyze−(x2+y2+z2)/2}. Show that f is a probability density, and that under f every pair of coordinates is N2(0,I). So the three variables are pairwise jointly normal and pairwise independent. Show that they are not mutually independent and that (X,Y,Z) is not jointly normal. Which step of @thm-mvn-independence fails?

exr-mvn-partial-product.title: B2
exr-mvn-partial-product.html: Let Σ be positive definite. Show that the coefficient of Yj in the best linear predictor of Y1 from all the other entries is −ω1j/ω11. Deduce that ρ1j⋅rest2 equals the product of the coefficient of Yj for predicting Y1 and the coefficient of Y1 for predicting Yj, each from all the other variables.

exr-mvn-partial-zero.title: A1
exr-mvn-partial-zero.html: Show that ρ12⋅3=0 iff ρ12=ρ13ρ23. Find ρ12⋅3 when ρ12=0 and ρ13=ρ23=0.6, and interpret.

exr-mvn-precision-conditional.title: B5
exr-mvn-precision-conditional.html: With Ω=Σ−1 partitioned like Σ, show that 𝛍𝛍E(Y1∣Y2=y2)=μ1−Ω11−1Ω12(y2−μ2) and Cov(Y1∣Y2)=Ω11−1.

exr-mvn-precision-row.title: A2
exr-mvn-precision-row.html: In the setting of @eq-mvn-random-x-model, let Ω be the inverse of Cov((Y,X⊤)⊤). Show that the row of Ω belonging to Y is 𝛃(1,−β⊤)/σ2, where σ2=σY2(1−ρY⋅X2). So the regression coefficients and the error variance can be read off one row of the precision matrix.

exr-mvn-projection-independence.title: A2
exr-mvn-projection-independence.html: Let Y∼Nn(0,I) and let u be a unit vector. Show that u⊤Y and ‖Y−(u⊤Y)u‖2 are independent.

exr-mvn-random-walk.title: B3
exr-mvn-random-walk.html: Let Z1,…,Zn be independent N(0,1) and Sk=Z1+⋯+Zk. Show that (S1,…,Sn) is jointly normal with Cov(Sj,Sk)=min(j,k). Find the conditional distribution of Sj given Sn=s, and comment on its variance as a function of j.

exr-mvn-rank-deficient-independence.title: B2
exr-mvn-rank-deficient-independence.html: Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2I) with rank(X)=r<p, let G be a generalized inverse of X⊤X and M=XGX⊤. Show that the least squares estimate GX⊤Y and the residual vector (I−M)Y are independent, and that every estimable function 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β with 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤) has an estimate independent of the residual sum of squares.

exr-mvn-rank-one.title: B1
exr-mvn-rank-one.html: Let Z∼N(0,1) and Y=(Z, 2Z−1, 3−Z)⊤. Show that Y is normal, find 𝛍μ and Σ, and find the rank of Σ. Describe the set in which Y lies, and write it as the solution set of two linear equations.

exr-mvn-residual-leverage.title: A2
exr-mvn-residual-leverage.html: In @exm-mvn-ls-estimator, show that the ith residual is N(0,σ2(1−mii)), where mii is the ith diagonal entry of M, and that it is zero with probability one iff mii=1.

exr-mvn-rotation.title: B1
exr-mvn-rotation.html: Let Y∼Nn(μ1,σ2I) and let Q be an orthogonal matrix whose first row is n−1/21⊤. Show that the entries of V=QY are independent, with V1∼N(nμ,σ2) and Vi∼N(0,σ2) for i≥2. Show that ∑i(Yi−Y¯)2=∑i≥2Vi2, and conclude again that Y¯ and S2 are independent.

exr-mvn-sample-precision.title: B3
exr-mvn-sample-precision.html: Let D be an n×k data matrix whose columns are centred, and let S=D⊤D. Show, using @thm-proj-fwl and the partitioned inverse, that −w12/w11w22, computed from S−1=(wij), equals the correlation of the residuals of columns 1 and 2 after regression on the remaining columns.

exr-mvn-sign-flip-directions.title: B3
exr-mvn-sign-flip-directions.html: For the pair (Z,W) of @exm-mvn-sign-flip, find every a≠0 for which a1Z+a2W is normal. Hint: an equal mixture of N(0,v1) and N(0,v2) has fourth moment 32(v12+v22). Conclude that (Z,W) is normal along exactly two lines through the origin, the coordinate axes.

exr-mvn-singular-conditioning.title: B4
exr-mvn-singular-conditioning.html: Let (Y,X1,X2) be normal with positive definite covariance, and let Y2=(X1,X2,X1+X2)⊤. Show that Σ22 is singular. Using a generalized inverse, show that the conditional distribution of Y given Y2 from @thm-mvn-conditional coincides with its conditional distribution given (X1,X2).

exr-mvn-singular-density.title: B2
exr-mvn-singular-density.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with rank(Σ)=r<n, and use the notation of @prp-mvn-rank-representation. Show that 𝛍V=Q⊤(Y−μ) has a density on Rr, and that this density can be written as 𝛍𝛍(2π)−r/2(λ1⋯λr)−1/2exp⁡{−12(y−μ)⊤Σ+(y−μ)} with 𝛍y=μ+Qv, where Σ+=QΛ−1Q⊤ is the Moore–Penrose inverse.

exr-mvn-smallest-region.title: C1
exr-mvn-smallest-region.html: Let Y have density @eq-mvn-density, and let E={y:Δ2(y)≤q}. Show that every Borel set A with Pr(Y∈A)≥Pr(Y∈E) has volume at least that of E. Hint: compare ∫A∖Ef with ∫E∖Af.

exr-mvn-sum-difference.title: A1
exr-mvn-sum-difference.html: Let Y1,Y2 be independent N(μ,σ2). Show that Y1+Y2 and Y1−Y2 are independent. What if the variances differ?

exr-mvn-tangent.title: B2
exr-mvn-tangent.html: Show that for a bivariate normal density with |ρ|<1, the points of each contour ellipse at which the tangent is vertical lie on the line y=E(Y∣X=x). Explain the result in terms of the conditional density of Y given X=x.

exr-mvn-truncated-sign.title: B2
exr-mvn-truncated-sign.html: Let Z∼N(0,1) and, for c>0, let W=Z if |Z|≤c and W=−Z otherwise. Show that W∼N(0,1), that there is a c with Cov(Z,W)=0, and that (Z,W) is not jointly normal for any c.

lem-mvn-schur.html:
Let Σ be nonnegative definite and partitioned as above, and let G be any generalized inverse of Σ22. Then:

  1. C(Σ21)⊆C(Σ22), so Σ21=Σ22H for some matrix H;

  2. Σ12GΣ22=Σ12 and Σ22GΣ21=Σ21;

  3. Σ12GΣ21=H⊤Σ22H, which does not depend on the choice of G and is nonnegative definite.

The matrix Σ11⋅2=Σ11−Σ12Σ22−Σ21, the Schur complement of Σ22 in Σ, is therefore well defined. It is the partial covariance matrix of Y1 given Y2 in the sense of @thm-rv-blp.

lem-mvn-stack.html: If 𝛍Y1∼Nn1(μ1,Σ1) and 𝛍Y2∼Nn2(μ2,Σ2) are independent, then (Y1⊤,Y2⊤)⊤ is jointly normal with mean 𝛍𝛍(μ1⊤,μ2⊤)⊤ and block-diagonal covariance diag(Σ1,Σ2). Consequently, if also n1=n2, then 𝛍𝛍Y1+Y2∼N(μ1+μ2,Σ1+Σ2).

lem-mvn-univariate.html:
Let X∼N(μ,σ2) with σ2≥0.

  1. EesX=exp⁡(μs+12σ2s2) for every real s.

  2. A random variable whose moment generating function is exp⁡(μs+12σ2s2) on an interval around 0 has the N(μ,σ2) distribution.

  3. aX+b∼N(aμ+b,a2σ2), and if X1∼N(μ1,σ12) and X2∼N(μ2,σ22) are independent, then X1+X2∼N(μ1+μ2,σ12+σ22).

prp-mvn-best-predictor.html: Let Y be jointly normal and partitioned as above, and let 𝛍𝛍m(Y2)=μ1+Σ12Σ22−(Y2−μ2). For every function g with E‖g(Y2)‖2<∞, E‖Y1−g(Y2)‖2=tr(Σ11⋅2)+E‖m(Y2)−g(Y2)‖2. So m(Y2) minimizes the mean squared prediction error over all predictors, it equals the best linear predictor of @thm-proj-blp (entry by entry, when Σ22 is positive definite), and the minimum is tr(Σ11⋅2).

prp-mvn-mahalanobis.html: If 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with Σ positive definite, then Δ2(Y) has the chi-squared distribution with n degrees of freedom, χ2(n), which is χ2(n,0) in the notation of @def-qf-noncentral-chisq. So the ellipsoid {y:Δ2(y)≤q}, where q is the 1−α quantile of χ2(n), has probability exactly 1−α.

prp-mvn-partial-meaning.html:
In the setting of @def-mvn-partial-correlation:

  1. Σ11⋅2 is the covariance matrix of the prediction errors 𝛍𝛍W=Y1−μ1−Σ12Σ22−(Y2−μ2), and W is uncorrelated with Y2. If Σ22 is positive definite, the ith entry of 𝛍𝛍μ1+Σ12Σ22−1(Y2−μ2) is the best linear prediction of Yi from Y2 in the sense of @thm-rv-blp(c), so ρij⋅2 is the correlation of the two prediction errors Wi and Wj.

  2. If Y is jointly normal, ρij⋅2 is the correlation of Yi and Yj in their conditional distribution given Y2=y2, the same for every y2. Moreover ρij⋅2=0 iff Yi and Yj are conditionally independent given Y2.

prp-mvn-partial-recursion.title: Recursion
prp-mvn-partial-recursion.html: Let S be a set of indices and k∉S∪{1,2} one more. Suppose σ11⋅S, σ22⋅S and σkk⋅S are positive and |ρ1k⋅S|<1, |ρ2k⋅S|<1. Then σ12⋅Sk=σ12⋅S−σ1k⋅Sσ2k⋅Sσkk⋅S,ρ12⋅Sk=ρ12⋅S−ρ1k⋅Sρ2k⋅S(1−ρ1k⋅S2)(1−ρ2k⋅S2). With S empty this is @eq-mvn-partial-recursion.

prp-mvn-precision.title: Partial correlations from the precision matrix
prp-mvn-precision.title_html: Partial correlations from the precision matrix
prp-mvn-precision.html: Let Σ be positive definite and Ω=Σ−1=(ωij). The partial correlation of Yi and Yj given all the other entries of Y is ρij⋅rest=−ωijωiiωjj, and the conditional variance of Yi given all the others is 1/ωii.

prp-mvn-rank-representation.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) with rank(Σ)=r≥1, and let Σ=QΛQ⊤, where Q is n×r with orthonormal columns and Λ=diag(λ1,…,λr) holds the positive eigenvalues. Put 𝛍W=Λ−1/2Q⊤(Y−μ). Then W∼Nr(0,Ir), and 𝛍Y=μ+QΛ1/2Wwith probability one.

thm-mvn-conditional.title: Conditional distribution
thm-mvn-conditional.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) be partitioned as above, let G be a generalized inverse of Σ22, and put B=Σ12G. Then:

  1. 𝛍𝛍W=Y1−μ1−B(Y2−μ2) is independent of Y2 and W∼Nn1(0,Σ11⋅2);

  2. the conditional distribution of Y1 given Y2=y2 is 𝛍𝛍Y1∣Y2=y2 ∼ Nn1(μ1+Σ12Σ22−(y2−μ2), Σ11−Σ12Σ22−Σ21),{#eq-mvn-conditional}

        and for \( \y_2 \) in \( \bmu_2+\C(\bSigma_{22}) \), where \( \Y_2 \) lies with probability
    one, the conditional mean does not depend on the choice of \( \G \);

  3. if Σ is positive definite, then Σ22−=Σ22−1, Σ11⋅2 is positive definite, Σ11⋅2−1 is the leading n1×n1 block of Σ−1, and detΣ=detΣ22detΣ11⋅2.

thm-mvn-density.title: Density
thm-mvn-density.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ).

  1. If Σ is positive definite, Y has the density 𝛍𝛍f(y)=(2π)−n/2det(Σ)−1/2exp⁡{−12(y−μ)⊤Σ−1(y−μ)},y∈Rn.{#eq-mvn-density}

  2. Conversely, a random vector with density @eq-mvn-density, for some positive definite Σ, is 𝛍Nn(μ,Σ).

  3. If Σ is singular, Y has no density on Rn.

thm-mvn-existence.title: Existence and the representation \bmu+\A\Z
thm-mvn-existence.title_html: Existence and the representation 𝛍μ+AZ
thm-mvn-existence.html:
Let Z1,…,Zm be independent N(0,1) variables and Z=(Z1,…,Zm)⊤.

  1. Z∼Nm(0,Im).

  2. For any n×m matrix A and 𝛍μ∈Rn, 𝛍Y=μ+AZ is multivariate normal with mean 𝛍μ and covariance AA⊤.

  3. For every 𝛍μ∈Rn and every nonnegative definite n×n matrix Σ there is a random vector with the 𝛍Nn(μ,Σ) distribution, for example 𝛍μ+Σ1/2Z with m=n.

No other matrices occur: the covariance matrix of a normal vector is nonnegative definite.

thm-mvn-independence.title: Independence
thm-mvn-independence.html:
Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ) be partitioned into blocks Y=(Y1⊤,…,Yk⊤)⊤, with 𝛍μ and Σ=(Σij) partitioned to match.

  1. The blocks Y1,…,Yk are mutually independent iff Σij=Cov(Yi,Yj)=0 for all i≠j.

  2. In particular, Y1 and Y2 are independent iff Cov(Y1,Y2)=0, and the scalar entries Y1,…,Yn are mutually independent iff Σ is diagonal.

thm-mvn-linear.title: Affine transformations
thm-mvn-linear.html: Let 𝛍Y∼Nn(μ,Σ), let A be any m×n matrix and b∈Rm. Then 𝛍AY+b∼Nm(Aμ+b, AΣA⊤).

thm-mvn-mgf.title: Moment generating function
thm-mvn-mgf.html:
A random vector Y is 𝛍Nn(μ,Σ) iff 𝛍MY(t)=exp⁡(t⊤μ+12t⊤Σt)for every t∈Rn.{#eq-mvn-mgf}

Consequently the distribution of a normal vector is determined by its mean vector and covariance matrix.
